body:
Alright this is a first pass at a review.

In general, it would be good if you could communicate how you expect and enduser to make use of this functionality. Either in form of examples in the docstrings, in the form of a tutorial, or in form of an issue in case you plan to add more features building up on top of this. Without an overview of your plans for this it is hard to see what you are going for.

In short:
- what does a workflow involving these methods look like?
- do you plan to add more public API classes/methods building up on this?

Depending on your answers to the above, this will also be of interest to #1033 which is laying the foundation for the addition of 4- and 8-fold symmetry aware two-body tensors. (see the description of that PR, too)

In general this looks good to me :+1: 
I left some comments and besides those below just a few additions:

- this PR needs a release note
- you say in the description that you will add routines to more tightly couple to `ElectronicEnergy` in the future. Since this PR has been open for a while, we have added a `Tensor` class in the meantime. Given my comments on `sparse.SparseArray` below, it might be worthwhile considering supporting `Tensor` as the input type in addition to numpy arrays unless there is a good reason _not_ to support sparse arrays.
- This will likely simplify the integration with the rest of the stack down the road.

Besides the missing reno this looks good to me.

@woodsp-ibm please also have a look when you have time

Seems it finally worked out with the release note.
